classification.difficultyReason: The median is given and the student must work backwards to x. They have to reason about where x sits among 4, 8, 12 and 20, with no scaffolding. Part b is simple: x must be the middle value, so x = 10. Parts a and c are harder because the answer is a range, not a single value. The student must see that any x at or below 8 (or at or above 12) leaves the median unchanged, and must handle the boundary value correctly. This is more than the single-step mean correction in p19-q14, which is a routine linked procedure. It is less than p22-q8, which asks for several constructions, adding a score, and an explanation of why adding a score differs from replacing one. It also needs no multi-statistic constraint satisfaction like p27-q14.
